#### 1. immunodeficiency 47  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.448)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8980692)

**Proposed mechanism:** DDRGK1 (HGNC:28078) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0009940); ATP6AP1 (HGNC:18090) —DISRUPTS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0009940); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0009940) —LEADS_TO→ lysosomal acidification (GO:0005704); lysosomal acidification (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Osteopetrosis (HP:0004771); lysosomal acidification (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). Loss-of-function mutations in DDRGK1 and ATP6AP1 disrupt the assembly and function of the V-ATPase, a key component of the lysosomal acidification machinery. Impaired lysosomal acidification leads to the accumulation of undigested material and cellular dysfunction, manifesting as Osteopetrosis and various forms of Immunodeficiency.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that loss-of-function mutations in DDRGK1 and ATP6AP1 do not independently or synergistically affect V-ATPase function or lysosomal acidification in cellular models. Alternatively, identification of a distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathway driving each disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in gnomAD within the coding regions of DDRGK1 and ATP6AP1 that do not segregate with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of impaired lysosomal acidification due to defects in DDRGK1 and ATP6AP1 could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both Osteopetrosis and Immunodeficiency 47, potentially involving strategies to restore lysosomal pH or enhance lysosomal function.
